cards.text: Every year, Jesus' parents go to Jerusalem for the Feast of the Passover. EVERY year, friend. I sat in a junk drawer for YEARS and couldn't make it three feet to the counter, and these folks make that trip like clockwork.

cards.question: Jesus' parents go up to Jerusalem for the Feast again, just like always. This time, Jesus is ___ years old.

cards.text: When the feast days are over, everybody packs up and heads for home. Everybody except the boy Jesus, who stays behind in Jerusalem.

cards.question: As they head for home, Jesus' parents know He stayed behind in Jerusalem.

cards.text: His parents figure He's somewhere in the traveling group, so they keep walking for a WHOLE day. It's like three cars pulling out after the office party, and every car is SURE he's riding in one of the other two.

cards.question: After a day on the road, Jesus' parents start looking for Him. Where do they look first?

cards.text: They go through the relatives. They go through the friends. And Jesus is NOT. THERE.

cards.question: Jesus isn't anywhere in the traveling group. What do His parents do?

answers.text: Go back to Jerusalem to search
Wait on the road for Him

cards.question: Back in Jerusalem, the search goes on. His parents finally find Jesus after ___ days.
After three days, where do Jesus' parents finally find Him?
There in the temple courts, Jesus is sitting among the teachers. What is He doing?

answers.text: Reading a scroll aloud to them
Leading them all in a psalm

cards.question: Everyone in the temple courts who hears Jesus is ___ at His understanding and His answers.

cards.text: When His parents see Him, they are astonished. I bet those three days felt like forever, and friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, so I don't throw the word forever around lightly.
His mother asks, “Child, why have You done this to us?” Then she tells Him, “Your father and I have been anxiously searching for You.”

cards.question: Jesus asks His parents why they were looking for Him. Where does He say He had to be?
Jesus' parents understand what He means when He says He had to be in His Father's house.

cards.text: Then Jesus goes down to Nazareth with His parents. The boy who just astounded the teachers takes the road home with His family.

cards.question: Back home in Nazareth, Jesus is obedient to His parents.
After everything that happened in Jerusalem, Jesus' mother ___ all these things in her heart.
Back in Nazareth, Jesus grows in wisdom and stature. Who does He grow in favor with?

findings.problem: The opening card brings in Jesus and His parents without saying who they are. Mary and Joseph are named in the passage right before this one, and a short tag would give the baker context, such as Jesus' parents, Mary and Joseph, or the young Jesus.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The second sentence repeats what the baker already knows (Jesus astounded the teachers and is going home with His family). It adds no new moment and has none of Papa Dorin's voice. It reads like a pleasant restatement, not his storytelling.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "forgets" and "ignores" don't match the tone of "treasures". They read as obviously wrong next to "in her heart" ("forgets all these things in her heart" barely makes sense), so the right answer stands out. Believable wrong answers would be words like "questions" or "weighs".

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
